question: Can a faraway planet have a lopsided sky?
happened: Last week we guessed about ships in a narrow sea. Fewer got through. This week, scientists used the Webb space telescope to look at a hot planet called WASP-17b. Its sky is lopsided: it reaches farther on one side than the other.

hero.caption: A planet with an uneven edge

steps.title: Hot side
steps.text: One side of the planet is warmed by its star.

steps.title: Wind blows
steps.text: Winds carry heat toward the darker side.

steps.title: Lopsided sky
steps.text: The sky reaches farther on one side than the other.

home.text: Sunshine warms our planet too. Wind moves warm air to cooler places. That is part of why the weather changes where you live.

find_it.text: WASP-17b is about 1,300 light-years away. That is much too far to visit! Draw what you think its sky looks like.

try_it.title: Warm side, cool side
steps: Go outside on a sunny day with a grown-up.
Touch a wall in the sun. Then touch a wall in the shade.
Which side feels warmer? Why do you think so?

questions: Which side of our home feels warmer in the afternoon?
What do you think wind does to warm air?
talk.tip: Today's skill is compare: look at two things and say how they differ. Ask "what do you notice?" Don't correct; add one more detail.

next_week: Will it be sunny or cloudy where we live next Saturday? Write or draw your guess, then check next week.
